d: Textures and decals are images you can place on object surfaces.
h:
A Texture is an image you can place on any face of a part or union that repeats both horizontally and vertically on the size of the surface. In contrast, a Decal is an image that stretches to fit the area of a part or union's surface. After you add a Texture or Decal object to a part or union, you can:

  • Change the texture or decal Color3 property to set a color tint using RGB color codes.

  • Change the texture or decal Transparency property to a value between the default of 0 (fully visible) and 1 (invisible).

  • For a texture, set its scale and offset.

Create textures or decals

To create a texture or decal, you must add either a Texture or Decal object to a part or union. You can import images for textures and decals to Studio for use between games, and distribute them to the Creator Store. Once you import the image, Studio assigns it a unique asset ID.

Every texture or decal image that you create and import to Roblox must adhere to the Community Rules and Terms of Use.

To add a texture or decal to a part or union:

  1. In the Explorer window, add a Texture or Decal to the part or union. An empty texture or decal object displays on the part or union with orange outlining.

  2. In the Properties window, navigate to the Face property and choose a face (Top, Bottom, Front, Back, Left, or Right).

  3. OPTIONAL To assist in choosing the correct face, right-click the part/union and select Show Orientation Indicator. This displays a circle 🅕, a blue line attached to the object's front face, and a green arrow that points in the direction of the object's top face.

  4. Select the ColorMapContent property and apply an image through any of the following methods:

  5. Select any texture or decal you've uploaded previously.

  6. Enter an asset ID into the field.

  7. OPTIONAL Set a color tint by clicking the small box to the left of the Color3 property or by entering a RGB color code.

Customize textures

Unlike decals, textures provide further functionality to scale, offset, and animate the source image.

Scale textures

The size of the part doesn't affect the texture. Instead, scaling a part only increases or decreases the number of times the texture repeats.

The StudsPerTileU and StudsPerTileV properties determine the size of each "tile" in studs. StudsPerTileU determines the texture's horizontal size while StudsPerTileV determines the texture's vertical size.

Offset textures

If you want more control over a texture's position, offset the texture by adjusting the OffsetStudsU (horizontal) and OffsetStudsV (vertical) properties. This is also helpful for animation.

Animate textures

Using TweenService, you can tween texture properties like OffsetStudsU and StudsPerTileV to achieve animated surfaces. For example, if you apply two fog textures to one container and animate them with the following script, you can achieve the appearance of a layered moving fog.

local TweenService = game:GetService("TweenService")

local texture1 = script.Parent.Texture1
local texture2 = script.Parent.Texture2

local tweenInfo1 = TweenInfo.new(8, Enum.EasingStyle.Sine, Enum.EasingDirection.InOut, -1)
local tween1 = TweenService:Create(texture1, tweenInfo1, {OffsetStudsV=50})
local tweenInfo2 = TweenInfo.new(7, Enum.EasingStyle.Sine, Enum.EasingDirection.InOut, -1, true)
local tween2 = TweenService:Create(texture2, tweenInfo2, {OffsetStudsU=50, StudsPerTileU=55, StudsPerTileV=45})

tween1:Play()
tween2:Play()

Texture streaming

Texture streaming dynamically loads textures based on distance and camera view, which lets you use textures more freely without worrying about scaling across devices. The engine loads baseline-quality textures first, in order of importance, and then progressively raises the quality of each texture up to the memory available on the device. Texture streaming is enabled automatically, so you don't have to take any action to benefit from it.

Benefits

  • Faster perceived load times and smaller downloads: Textures appear almost immediately at a baseline quality, and the engine downloads only the detail it needs, compressing it both in transit and on the local disk cache.
  • Higher quality where it matters: The engine continuously estimates how important each object is, such as by how much screen space it occupies, and uses the memory budget on those textures so that the most prominent objects get the highest detail.
  • Fewer out-of-memory crashes: Because the engine stays within a memory budget and can lower texture quality when memory runs low, players are much less likely to crash from texture memory spikes.

Texture streaming works with MeshPart (skinned and unskinned), SurfaceAppearance, Texture, Decal, MaterialVariant, Beam, ParticleEmitter, and the base materials applied to PartOperation and BasePart instances.

Best practices

  • Favor unique, individual textures over texture atlases unless the atlas is applied to batchable parts; requesting a high resolution for one texture in an atlas streams in the entire atlas at that resolution.
  • Use near-uniform texel density in your UV-mapped meshes so that the engine can select the best resolution for each texture.
  • Continue to manage texture memory carefully for instance types that texture streaming doesn't support yet.

kid.simple: Textures and decals let you stick images onto the faces of parts, like a brick pattern on a wall or a poster on a sign. A Decal stretches one image to cover a whole face, while a Texture repeats the image over and over like tiles. Textures can also be moved and scaled, and even animated with code to make things like flowing water or drifting fog. This is one of the easiest ways to make plain blocks look detailed.
kid.analogy: A Decal is like a single sticker stretched to fit a box lid. A Texture is like wallpaper: the same pattern repeats across the whole wall, and a bigger wall just gets more repeats.
keyPoints: A Decal stretches its image to fill one face. A Texture repeats its image across the face.
Add a Decal or Texture as a child of a part or union, then choose which face it goes on with the `Face` property: Top, Bottom, Front, Back, Left or Right.
Set the image with `ColorMapContent`, using an image you uploaded or its asset ID.
`Color3` tints the image and `Transparency` goes from 0 (fully visible) to 1 (invisible).
For Textures, `StudsPerTileU` and `StudsPerTileV` set how many studs wide and tall each repeat of the image is.
`OffsetStudsU` and `OffsetStudsV` slide the image sideways or up and down. Changing them over time with TweenService animates the surface.
Texture streaming loads simple versions of images first and sharper ones later, automatically, so games load faster and crash less.
Right-click a part and choose Show Orientation Indicator to see which face is Front (blue line) and which is Top (green arrow).

terms.Decal: An image stuck to one face of a part that stretches to fit. A square image on a 10 x 2 stud face gets squashed to fit that long thin shape.
terms.Texture: An image stuck to one face that repeats like tiles. On a 10 stud wide face with 2 studs per tile, it repeats 5 times across.
terms.face: One flat side of a part. A block has 6 faces: Top, Bottom, Front, Back, Left and Right.
terms.union: A shape made by combining parts with solid modeling.
terms.tint: A color mixed over the image. A Color3 of (255, 255, 255) keeps the original colors, while (255, 0, 100) gives it a pink-red look.
terms.U and V: Names for the two directions across a flat image. U is horizontal (left-right) and V is vertical (up-down).
terms.StudsPerTile: How big one copy of the image is, in studs. On an 8 stud wide wall, `StudsPerTileU = 2` shows 4 copies across and `StudsPerTileU = 4` shows 2.
terms.offset: How far the image is slid from its starting spot, in studs. `OffsetStudsU = 0.5` shifts the pattern half a stud sideways.
terms.tween: A smooth change of a value from one number to another over time, like sliding an offset from 0 to 50 over 8 seconds.
terms.streaming (texture): Loading images little by little: blurry first, then sharper as memory allows.
terms.asset ID: The number Roblox gives an uploaded image so you can use it anywhere.
terms.texture atlas: One big image that holds many small images packed together.
terms.texel density: How many image pixels cover each stud of a surface. Keeping it even makes everything look equally sharp.

example.title: Make a scrolling conveyor belt texture
example.place: Script inside a long anchored Part named Conveyor (server Script)
example.code:
local TweenService = game:GetService("TweenService")

local belt = script.Parent  -- a part, for example 4 studs wide and 20 studs long

local stripes = Instance.new("Texture")
stripes.Face = Enum.NormalId.Top
stripes.ColorMapContent = Content.fromAssetId(0) -- replace 0 with your image's asset ID
stripes.StudsPerTileU = 4   -- each copy is 4 studs wide (1 copy across a 4 stud belt)
stripes.StudsPerTileV = 2   -- each copy is 2 studs long (10 copies along 20 studs)
stripes.Parent = belt

-- Slide the image 2 studs (one full tile) every 0.5 seconds, forever
local info = TweenInfo.new(0.5, Enum.EasingStyle.Linear, Enum.EasingDirection.In, -1)
local tween = TweenService:Create(stripes, info, { OffsetStudsV = 2 })
tween:Play()
explain: We create a Texture and put it on the Top face of the belt part.
`Content.fromAssetId` sets the image. Put in the asset ID of a stripe image you uploaded.
On a 20 stud long belt, `StudsPerTileV = 2` repeats the image 20 / 2 = 10 times along its length.
The tween slides `OffsetStudsV` from 0 to 2 in 0.5 seconds. Since 2 studs is exactly one tile, the jump back to 0 looks seamless.
A repeat count of -1 means the tween loops forever, so the stripes keep scrolling. That looks like 2 / 0.5 = 4 studs per second of movement.
This only changes the look. It does not push players. A real conveyor would also need physics, such as setting the part's `AssemblyLinearVelocity`.

watchOut: Using a Decal when you want a repeating pattern makes the image look stretched and blurry on big walls. Use a Texture instead.
Your image may appear on the wrong side. Check the `Face` property and use Show Orientation Indicator to find Front and Top.
Resizing a part does not resize a Texture's image. It only changes how many times it repeats. Change `StudsPerTileU` and `StudsPerTileV` to resize the image.
Images you upload must follow the Community Rules and Terms of Use, or they can be removed.
